description.en-US:
Le dictionnaire de la langue fran\xE7aise d'\xC9mile Littr\xE9,
complet et enti\xE8rement gratuit, consultable hors-ligne.

Widget d'\xE9cran d'accueil \xAB Mot du jour \xBB, et mot du jour expos\xE9 aux
autres applications (tuile de Reader's Launcher).
78 599 entr\xE9es avec d\xE9finitions, \xE9tymologies et citations.
Recherche instantan\xE9e, mot du jour, favoris, renvois crois\xE9s
cliquables, mode sombre. Aucune connexion internet requise.
Donn\xE9es lexicographiques sous licence CC BY-SA 3.0
(Fran\xE7ois Gannaz, littre.org).

Reader's Launcher turns the home screen into a single column of words. No icons,
no colours, no wallpaper: white on black, or black on white — flip between the two
with a double tap, from the "Reader's theme" quick-settings tile, or in settings.

* The home screen is one fixed page that never scrolls. Tiles are plain text: an app,
  or a category that opens a text list of apps.
* A grid of 3 to 5 squares pinned at the bottom holds the unavoidable apps (phone,
  messages…) with their icons rendered as monochrome glyphs.
* Built-in widgets: clock; weather (Open-Meteo, no account, tap for five days);
  agenda (next event, swipe for the following ones); tasks (first task of a list
  from Reader's Tasks or Tasks.org, swipe for the following ones, tick to complete,
  + to add). Standard app widgets can be added too.
* Swipe up for the alphabetical app list with search and the usual long-press
  actions (add to home, category, rename, hide, app info, uninstall).
* Swipe up and hold on the home screen for a text list of recently used apps.
* Swipe down for notifications. Export and import the whole setup as a JSON file.
* Two books beside the home screen: swipe right or left to open one (EPUB, MOBI, FB2,
  plain text), tap to turn pages; each book reopens where you stopped.
* English by default; French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian follow the
  device language.

Serif, sans or monospace; three text sizes; left or centred. No ads, no tracking.

Reader's Tasks shows the open tasks of a CalDAV list — Infomaniak, Nextcloud,
Tasks.org Cloud, Radicale, any server that stores VTODO — as plain text, white on
black or black on white. Tick a box to complete, tap the line at the bottom to add,
long press for rename, due tomorrow, delete. "show n done" brings completed tasks
back so a box ticked by mistake can be reopened. Lists can be hidden and reordered.

It is the task app behind the tasks tile of Reader's Launcher: the launcher reads
and writes the lists directly, with no permission prompt, since both apps are signed
with the same key. The desktop twin for Linux lives at
github.com/funkypitt/readers-tasks.

Serif, sans or monospace; three text sizes. No account with the app itself, no
tracking: your server, your app password, stored on the phone only.
